subject: math
cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software

items.prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure $52^\circ$ and $61^\circ$. Find the measure of the third angle.

steps: The interior angles of any triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: A right triangle has one angle of $90^\circ$ and another angle of $35^\circ$. Find the measure of the third angle.

steps: The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel and are cut by a transversal. One angle measures $124^\circ$. Find the measure of its alternate interior angle.

steps: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are congruent (equal in measure).
The alternate interior angle has the same measure as the given angle.
Therefore the alternate interior angle measures $124^\circ$.

items.prompt: Lines $p$ and $q$ are parallel and are cut by a transversal. One angle measures $78^\circ$. Find the measure of its co-interior (same-side interior) angle.

steps: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, co-interior (same-side interior) angles are supplementary, so they sum to $180^\circ$.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure $48^\circ$ and $66^\circ$. Find the measure of the exterior angle adjacent to the third vertex.

steps: By the exterior-angle theorem, an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
Add the two remote interior angles: $48^\circ + 66^\circ = 114^\circ$.

items.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has angles measuring $43^\circ$ and $82^\circ$. Triangle $DEF$ has angles measuring $82^\circ$ and $55^\circ$. Are the two triangles similar? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Yes, the triangles are similar by AA.

steps: Find the third angle of triangle $ABC$: $180^\circ - 43^\circ - 82^\circ = 55^\circ$. Its angles are $43^\circ, 82^\circ, 55^\circ$.
Find the third angle of triangle $DEF$: $180^\circ - 82^\circ - 55^\circ = 43^\circ$. Its angles are $82^\circ, 55^\circ, 43^\circ$.
Both triangles have angles $43^\circ, 55^\circ, 82^\circ$, so at least two pairs of angles are congruent.
By the angle-angle (AA) criterion, the triangles are similar.

items.prompt: Lines $r$ and $s$ are parallel and are cut by a transversal. A pair of corresponding angles measure $(3x + 14)^\circ$ and $(5x - 6)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.

steps: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are congruent, so set the expressions equal: $3x + 14 = 5x - 6$.

items.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. An alternate interior angle measures $59^\circ$, and that angle is one angle of a triangle whose second angle measures $73^\circ$. Find the third angle of the triangle.

steps: The alternate interior angle equals $59^\circ$ (alternate interior angles are congruent), so one angle of the triangle is $59^\circ$.

items.prompt: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel and are cut by a transversal. Two co-interior (same-side interior) angles measure $(2x + 25)^\circ$ and $(4x + 5)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$.

steps: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles formed by parallel lines are supplementary, so they sum to $180^\circ$: $(2x + 25) + (4x + 5) = 180$.

items.prompt: The exterior angle at one vertex of a triangle measures $128^\circ$. One of the two remote interior angles measures $51^\circ$. Find the other remote interior angle.

steps: By the exterior-angle theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $128^\circ = 51^\circ + (\text{other remote angle})$.
The other remote interior angle measures $77^\circ$.

items.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, the angles measure $(2x + 5)^\circ$, $(3x - 10)^\circ$, and $(x + 35)^\circ$. Find the value of $x$ and the measure of each angle.

steps: The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$: $(2x + 5) + (3x - 10) + (x + 35) = 180$.

items.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines $\ell$ and $m$. The alternate exterior angle on one side measures $(7x - 9)^\circ$, and the angle that corresponds to it on line $m$ measures $(5x + 21)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of each angle.

steps: An alternate exterior angle and a corresponding angle to it that share the same position are congruent across the parallel lines, so set the expressions equal: $7x - 9 = 5x + 21$.

items.prompt: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. An alternate interior angle measures $64^\circ$ and is one base angle of a triangle. The exterior angle at the opposite vertex (formed by extending one side) measures $137^\circ$. Find the third interior angle of the triangle.

steps: The alternate interior angle is congruent to its pair, so one base angle of the triangle is $64^\circ$.
By the exterior-angle theorem, the exterior angle of $137^\circ$ equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, one of which is the $64^\circ$ angle.
Let the third interior angle (the other remote angle) be $y$: $64^\circ + y = 137^\circ$.

The vertex where the exterior angle of $137^\circ$ is formed has interior angle $180^\circ - 137^\circ = 43^\circ$. Check: $64^\circ + 73^\circ + 43^\circ = 180^\circ$. The third interior angle (at that vertex) measures $43^\circ$.

items.prompt: Triangle $PQR$ has angles $(4x)^\circ$, $(5x)^\circ$, and $(9x)^\circ$. Triangle $STU$ has two angles measuring $40^\circ$ and $50^\circ$. Determine whether the two triangles are similar, and justify your answer.
items.answer: Yes, the triangles are similar by AA (both have angles $40^\circ$, $50^\circ$, and $90^\circ$).

steps: For triangle $PQR$, the angles sum to $180^\circ$: $4x + 5x + 9x = 180$, so $18x = 180$ and $x = 10$.
For triangle $STU$, the third angle is $180^\circ - 40^\circ - 50^\circ = 90^\circ$, so its angles are $40^\circ$, $50^\circ$, $90^\circ$.
Both triangles have angles $40^\circ$, $50^\circ$, and $90^\circ$, so two pairs of angles are congruent.
By the angle-angle (AA) criterion, the triangles are similar.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A same-side interior (co-interior) angle measures $(6x - 4)^\circ$, and the corresponding angle to its partner measures $(2x + 16)^\circ$. Set up and solve for $x$, then find the measure of the same-side interior angle $(6x - 4)^\circ$.

steps: Let the two same-side interior angles be the $(6x - 4)^\circ$ angle and its partner. The partner's corresponding angle is $(2x + 16)^\circ$, and corresponding angles are congruent, so the partner same-side interior angle also measures $(2x + 16)^\circ$.
Substitute $x = 21$ into $(6x - 4)$: $6(21) - 4 = 126 - 4 = 122^\circ$. The same-side interior angle measures $122^\circ$.
